title: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon, its strongest model, built for long agentic jobs, deep science and cyber defense
summary: Google made Gemini 4 Carbon available to developers, enterprises, scientists and consumers on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, calling it its strongest model, with frontier performance in cybersecurity and long-horizon agentic work across knowledge work, software engineering and scientific reasoning. Google says Carbon ranks #1 on CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity’s WANDR and Zapier’s AutomationBench at more than 2X lower cost per task than the next best external model. It is previewing /swarm in Google Antigravity, which turns a single prompt into a coordinated team of agents. API pricing is an introductory $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, rising to $4 and $20 after November 30. Google says Carbon passed 92% of tasks on its 375-task agentic honesty benchmark, versus 70% for Argon, and it is rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search.

title: S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures climb as CoreWeave’s results calm AI spending jitters
summary: Reuters reported Wednesday, November 11, 2026, that at 6:39 a.m. ET, S&P 500 E-minis gained 65 points, or 0.86%, Nasdaq 100 E-minis added 527.5 points, or 1.9%, and Dow E-minis rose 58 points, or 0.11%. Reuters said equities have been caught in a tug of war this week between worries over slower data-center deployment, higher interest rates and Nvidia’s troubles, and an appetite to buy the dip. Investors also parsed the terms Anthropic set Tuesday for its IPO, which aims for a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion. In Europe, the STOXX 600 rose 0.4%, within striking distance of its August record high.

title: CoreWeave surges premarket after raising its 2026 revenue outlook and promising profit in 2028
summary: Investing.com reported Wednesday, November 11, 2026, that CoreWeave shares surged 13.7% in premarket trading after third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion topped expectations of $3.55 billion and its adjusted loss of $0.95 a share beat the $1.16 forecast. The AI cloud provider raised 2026 revenue guidance to $13 billion to $13.3 billion and said its revenue backlog reached a record $133 billion, up 138% from a year earlier. It cited about $9 billion in expected customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months and said it does not intend to issue additional parent-level unsecured debt through 2027. Executives said they expect adjusted profitability in the first half of 2028. CNBC noted the shares are still down 65% from their May highs.

title: Nvidia rebounds about 5% before the bell after two sessions that erased roughly $430 billion
summary: Investing.com reported Wednesday, November 11, 2026, that Nvidia shares climbed 4.9% ahead of the opening bell, joining a broader chip rally as CoreWeave’s stronger outlook eased concerns about demand for AI infrastructure. Reuters put the premarket gain at 5.2% and said the stock had shed about $430 billion in the previous two sessions amid questions about CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a businesswoman alleged to be a Chinese spy. Advanced Micro Devices gained 6.4%, Intel added 6.2% and Broadcom advanced 4.2%, according to Investing.com. Nvidia reports third-quarter results on November 17.

title: Micron jumps with memory and chip stocks as the AI trade revives
summary: Investing.com reported Wednesday, November 11, 2026, that Micron Technology rose 6.5% in premarket trading as semiconductor stocks rallied after CoreWeave raised its full-year revenue forecast, a closely watched signal of AI infrastructure spending. Reuters, in its own premarket report, put Micron’s gain at 6.8% and said Marvell Technology was up 8%. Reuters also reported that technology stocks led gains across Asia, with Taiwan up 3.6% and South Korea up 2.6%.

title: New York opens its AI safety registration portal, putting OpenAI and Anthropic under new oversight
summary: TechCrunch reported Tuesday, November 10, 2026, that New York opened a registration portal that large frontier AI developers like Anthropic and OpenAI must use to register by January 1, 2027, when the RAISE Act kicks in. The law requires large frontier developers, those with more than $500 million in annual revenue, to publish safety frameworks, report critical safety incidents within 72 hours and issue public model transparency reports. A newly formed Office of Digital Innovation, Governance, Integrity, and Trust (DIGIT) will oversee the labs, with penalties up to $1 million for a first violation and $3 million for subsequent ones. Gov. Kathy Hochul also launched the New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research at SUNY Binghamton to independently evaluate advanced AI systems.

title: All seven Anthropic co-founders plan to sell about $250 million of stock each in the IPO
summary: TechCrunch reported Tuesday, November 10, 2026, that Anthropic’s updated S-1 shows each of its seven co-founders plans to sell 3,378,378 shares in the IPO. At the $74 midpoint of the $70–$78 range, each would take in just shy of $250 million; at the high end, just under $264 million. The filing hints at strong demand: board member Reed Hastings has indicated he wants to buy $300 million of shares through his donor-advised fund. After the sale each founder will own about 3.2% of outstanding Class A shares, roughly 22% collectively, and through supervoting Class F stock the founders will control 51.1% of the votes, TechCrunch said. Pricing is scheduled for November 18, with trading the following day, Quartz reported, citing Bloomberg.

title: Oura agrees to buy AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health for $625 million
summary: TechCrunch reported Tuesday, November 10, 2026, that Oura is acquiring Counsel Health, an AI-powered care platform that pairs a chat-based medical experience with licensed physicians, for $625 million. Counsel’s service was integrated into the Oura app in June, and the companies plan to expand into preventative, acute, specialty and chronic care. Counsel CEO Muthu Alagappan will join Oura as chief clinical AI officer along with the company’s 70 employees, per Bloomberg. The deal comes weeks after Oura postponed its IPO indefinitely; Oura also reported quarterly revenue up 153% year over year to $533 million.

title: OpenAI lets businesses claim and manage their profiles inside ChatGPT
summary: Reuters reported Tuesday, November 10, 2026, that OpenAI is launching “Businesses” in beta within ChatGPT, giving companies a way to claim and manage their profiles, update information and track how users engage with them on the chatbot. Through a tool called Business Hub, verified companies can update key details and add product feeds with pricing and availability, and see aggregated insights including mentions, views and website clicks. Reuters also reported that OpenAI is adding AI agents for U.S. e-commerce firms. TechCrunch said the move makes ChatGPT “just a little bit more like Google.”

title: MiniMax releases H3-Image, an open-weight model that generates and edits native 4K images
summary: Crypto Briefing reported Tuesday, November 10, 2026, that MiniMax released H3-Image on Hugging Face, through MiniMax Code and via its APIs. The 33.1-billion-parameter diffusion transformer handles both text-to-image generation and editing, producing native images of about 16 megapixels, including 4096×4096 and widescreen sizes up to 6272×2688. It needs about six sampling steps, accepts up to 16 reference images, and costs roughly $0.022 per 1K image and $0.069 per 4K image through the API. The catch: its community license excludes use in the US, the EU, the UK and South Korea, and larger companies need written authorization.

title: Nvidia posts open weights for Alpamayo 2 Edge, a 2-billion-parameter driving model that explains its moves
summary: IA Compa reported Tuesday, November 10, 2026, that Nvidia published the weights for Alpamayo 2 Edge on Hugging Face. It is a 2-billion-parameter vision-language-action model for autonomous driving that pairs a Cosmos 3 Edge reasoning backbone with a diffusion action expert to produce driving trajectories and explanations of them. It is optimized for Nvidia DRIVE AGX Thor and designed for 10 Hz in-vehicle operation, and the release includes deployment recipes and evaluation tools. The weights are under the OpenMDW-1.1 license and the code under Apache 2.0; Nvidia also released AlpaJudge, a human-calibrated evaluation and reward model.

title: Anthropic’s Claude can now join video calls and start the work while the meeting is still going
summary: TechCrunch reported Tuesday, November 10, 2026, that Anthropic launched Claude Meetings, which lets teams add Claude to a video call as a visible participant that drafts the plan being discussed, maps a timeline on a whiteboard, answers questions in the meeting chat and pulls information from connected work apps. Claude announces itself in the chat, won’t join calls with external guests unless an admin allows it, and leaves automatically if one joins. It is in beta on Team and Enterprise plans and works with Google Meet at launch. Anthropic also unveiled Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets in beta, and made Claude Data, formerly Claude Dashboards, generally available.

title: Ring launches a flying indoor security drone and a patrolling security robot for businesses
summary: Amazon said Tuesday, November 10, 2026, that Ring is launching Ring Robotics with two devices powered by AI Pilot, a system that maps a space, suggests patrol points and navigates around obstacles. Ring Drone Cam is a flying indoor security camera that flies preset routes when a Ring alarm or sensor is triggered, runs scheduled patrols and stays docked out of sight otherwise. Ring Rover Cam is an autonomous security robot for businesses with a periscope camera, two-way audio, a siren and continuous 4K video. Rover ships in the U.S. December 16 for $999.99, and the Drone Cam ships January 27, 2027, for $249.99; CNBC noted the drone’s ship date is pending FCC approval.

title: Adobe brings agents to Photoshop, Premiere and Firefly and opens a local MCP so outside chatbots can use its tools
summary: TechCrunch reported Tuesday, November 10, 2026, that Adobe announced a wave of AI features at its MAX event in Miami, including a local Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint that exposes features of Illustrator, Photoshop, After Effects and Premiere to chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Firefly is getting Builder, a prototyping tool in private beta, plus on-brand graphs, a video assembly tool and an agent that is proactive and always on. Photoshop gets relighting and generative style sliders, Premiere gets a professional color grading system and video object removal, and Lightroom can fix blinking eyes. Adobe VP Deepa Subramaniam said the company is “still figuring out where and when and how to draw the line” on what the MCP exposes.

title: A former Marine who isn’t a professional developer built Battle Buddy, an AI agent that helps veterans find their benefits
summary: Microsoft’s Source reported November 9, 2026, that Gary Crull, who served in the Marine Corps and the Army National Guard and now works as an analyst at the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, built Battle Buddy, an AI agent that helps veterans, families and caregivers make sense of federal, state and local benefits. He built it with low-code tools, training it on VA regulations and about 1,000 questions and answers drawn from veteran forums so it learns both what veterans ask and how they ask it. Some testers say they saved hours; others found information they had sought for more than a year. It is in open field testing, including at the VA Augusta Medical Center in Georgia. “Battle Buddy is made by veterans for veterans,” Crull says.

title: HKUST builds an AI “ASD Super Agent” to help families spot autism early and turn big goals into small daily steps
summary: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology announced on November 11, 2026, that a team led by Prof. Kani Chen developed ASD Super Agent, an AI platform for autism support that combines early screening, personalized intervention and continuous family follow-up. Parents can record short videos of a child’s daily activities and complete questionnaires to get a risk report to bring to professionals; in preliminary testing it scored an AUC of 0.92, and HKUST says more clinical validation will come before deployment. Parents can describe challenges like emotional regulation or communication and receive tailored suggestions drawn from more than 20 recognized intervention approaches. The team spoke with nearly 500 parents while building it, and the platform helps break long-term goals into manageable daily actions.

title: Acadiana Veteran Alliance holds a free Veterans Day ceremony at Moncus Park this morning
summary: The Acadiana Veteran Alliance invites the public to a Veterans Day ceremony on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, at 9 a.m. at the Veterans Memorial area of Moncus Park, 2913 Johnston St., Lafayette. The Moncus Park listing describes it as free and family-friendly, a morning of gratitude, reflection and recognition of veterans and their families. Presenting sponsors include Catalyst Bank, LFT Fiber, Chick-fil-A and Service Chevrolet, along with Lafayette Consolidated Government. The event is externally hosted, not produced by Moncus Park.

title: Aaron Lewis brings his Acoustic Origins Tour to the Cajundome Convention Center tonight
summary: Aaron Lewis: The Acoustic Origins Tour, presented by Doussan Music Group, comes to the Cajundome Convention Center, 444 Cajundome Blvd., Lafayette, on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. The Cajundome listing now shows doors at 5:30 p.m. and the show at 7 p.m. Tickets are on sale through Ticketmaster as SafeTix mobile tickets, and everyone needs a ticket. The venue is cashless and enforces a clear bag policy, with free parking at the Congress Street Gate 8 entrance.

title: Paul Thorn Band plays ‘Life Is Just A Vapor’ at Acadiana Center for the Arts Thursday
summary: The Paul Thorn Band performs Thursday, November 12, 2026, from 7:30 to 9:45 p.m. in the James Devin Moncus Theater at the Acadiana Center for the Arts, 101 W. Vermilion St., Lafayette. The AcA listing says his new album, Life Is Just A Vapor, is full of short, encouraging lines like “tough times don’t last, but tough people do.” It notes the title tune was inspired by his friend and mentor John Prine. The AcA box office opens one hour before showtime.

title: Cité des Arts opens Shakespeare’s ‘Othello’ with an opening-night gala Friday
summary: Cité des Arts, 109 Vine St., Lafayette, opens William Shakespeare’s Othello on Friday, November 13, 2026, with an opening-night gala at 6:30 p.m. and the show from 7:30 to 9:30 p.m. The listing describes it as the story of a noble Moorish general whose life and marriage are destroyed by manipulation, envy and treachery. General admission gala tickets, which include noshes and signature cocktails, are $35 plus a service fee.

title: Cajun Cup 10K and Farrel’s Mile start at Parc Sans Souci Saturday morning
summary: The Cajun Road Runners Club’s Cajun Cup 10K and Farrel’s Mile run Saturday, November 14, 2026, from Parc Sans Souci in downtown Lafayette, with the mile at 7:30 a.m. and the 10K at 8:05 a.m. The race is a fundraiser for the Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns cross country and track teams. Packet pickup is Friday from 9:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. at Geaux Run, or race morning from 6:30 to 7:45 a.m.; online registration closes Saturday at 7 a.m., and the 10K is $70 at packet pickup and race day. There’s also a shoe drive for Lafayette Catholic Services.

title: Second Saturday ArtWalk fills Downtown Lafayette with galleries, music and performances
summary: Downtown Lafayette’s November ArtWalk runs Saturday, November 14, 2026, from 5 to 9 p.m., rain or shine. Museums, independent galleries, studios, craft stores and art houses in the cultural district each host their own events featuring local artists and performers. Downtown Lafayette is partnering with Lafayette Arts & Fleas to highlight local talent. Metered street spaces are free after 5 p.m. on weekdays and all day on weekends, and the Parc-Auto du Centre-Ville garage at 121 E. Vermilion St. offers 530 spaces.
